name: lna-sparam-nf
description: S-parameter (S11/S21/S22/S12), k / |Delta| / mu stability, noise-figure and per-device operating-point bench for design/lna_stage1 (xschem npn13G2 cascode first stage, ideal behavioral L/C matching), at three points across the Ka-band downlink DRAFT band (17.7 / 19.45 / 21.2 GHz) plus a 1-100 GHz stability sweep, across the full HBT process x temperature x supply grid (2.75 V is a labelled excursion above row 17's 2.5 V ceiling).
claim: ideal-matching feasibility record; no spec row is claimed met; row 6 (k > 1) is reported, not claimed. The DUT is design/lna_stage1 (one cascode stage; row 2 assumes two) with IDEAL lossless L/C matching sized at the DRAFT band centre only to give the bench defined ports (spec row 1, the band, is still OPEN; no PDK inductor model exists, so no loss, Q or layout parasitic is represented). S11/S21/S22/NF are therefore feasibility figures, not compliance evidence for rows 2-5; k, |Delta| and mu are reported against row 6 without claiming it; the operating-point table is checked against row 17 and the model-card box, with the 2.75 V cells reported as an excursion.
netlist_provenance: schematic (design/lna_stage1.sch via xschem export, design/netlist/lna_stage1.spice, embedded verbatim in lna_stage1.spice; first-stage schematic, not a ratified design and never taken through layout)
analyses: let wk = real((1 - mag(w11)*mag(w11) - mag(w22)*mag(w22) + mag(wdel)*mag(wdel)) / (2*mag(w12)*mag(w21)))
let wunst = pos(1 - wk) + pos(wd - 1) - pos(1 - wk)*pos(wd - 1)

s21_db_mid.description: Sensitivity floor only (NOT a spec-compliance check): proves the PVT grid genuinely perturbs the stage's gain rather than silently simulating one corner for all requested points. Do not read this as 'meets the 20 dB DRAFT gain target' -- see the claim above.

nf_db_mid.description: Sensitivity floor only (NOT a spec-compliance check) -- see s21_db_mid's check for why.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated (ngspice, real npn13G2 VBIC model, no PDK inductor model used anywhere in this fixture -- see notes)
notes: DUT and provenance: design/lna_stage1.sch (xschem 3.4.4) -> design/netlist/lna_stage1.spice (design/export_netlist.sh) -> embedded verbatim between BEGIN/END markers in testbench/lna_stage1.spice (make_stage1_fixture.py; tests/test_lna_stage1.py fails if they differ). Topology argument and bias derivation: design/lna_stage1.md.

S-parameter method: power-wave injection via a Thevenin Z0=50 ohm source per port, toggled forward/reverse via alterparam+reset between two .ac calls in one deck (ngspice has no native .SP/S-parameter analysis). Full derivation: testbench/lna_ce_placeholder.spice's header comment (the method is unchanged in testbench/lna_stage1.spice).

Noise-figure method (CORRECTED, issue #22): the reference source Rs1 is noiseless (noisy=0) and its thermal noise is added analytically at an explicit T0 = 300.15 K (27 C): F = 1 + inoise_spectrum^2/(4*k*T0*Z0), NF_dB = 10*log10(F). inoise_spectrum is then the input-referred noise of the DUT plus the output load Rs2 and bias resistor Rbias, which stay noisy at each corner's .temp (output-load convention unchanged). T0 = 300.15 K matches sg13g2-lna's hbt-characterization convention (spec/porting-plan.md S1 'Ports directly'), not the IEEE textbook 290 K. The superseded record 20260912-034726-9204518 used a per-instance `Rs1 ... TEMP=27` override and wrongly claimed it pinned the source at exactly 300.15 K; in ngspice-46 an instance resistor temp=T generates noise at T + 300.15 K (measured by sim/hbt-kaband-characterization/run.py probe: 327.15 K at -40, 16.85, 27 and 125 C alike), so every nf_db_* value in that record is high by 27/300.15 = 0.0900 in linear F (not a constant dB offset). That is an observation on that simulator version, not a general statement. IMPORTANT: ngspice's .noise command's inoise_total/onoise_total vectors are BANDWIDTH-INTEGRATED RMS totals across the whole swept analysis range, not per-frequency spectral densities -- using them directly for a per-frequency NF overstates NF by roughly 10*log10(swept_bandwidth_Hz) (confirmed ~48 dB too high for this bench's 3.5 GHz sweep during development). This bench uses the separate noise2.inoise_spectrum vector (the 'Noise Spectral Density Curves' plot, distinct from the trailing 'Integrated Noise' plot) instead.

Frequency plan: `ac lin 3 17.7e9 21.2e9` for the S-parameter/NF/k/|Delta|/mu in-band set (17.7 / 19.45 / 21.2 GHz, the DRAFT band's edges and centre; spec row 1 is OPEN, so these are DRAFT points, not a ratified band) and a separate stability sweep `ac dec 100 1e9 1e11` (201 logarithmic points, 100 per decade, adjacent ratio 1.0233, about 1.5 GHz step at 63.6 GHz) in both directions for k, |Delta|, mu out to 100 GHz (row 6 asks for at least 63.6 GHz). The sweep does not cover < 1 GHz or > 100 GHz. A 3-point band set is a floor, not a continuous sweep: no S21/S11/NF flatness claim is made between the points.

Stability reporting: k = (1-|S11|^2-|S22|^2+|Delta|^2)/(2|S12 S21|), mu = (1-|S11|^2)/(|S22-Delta S11*|+|S12 S21|); any cell with k <= 1 or |Delta| >= 1 in band or in the sweep is labelled POTENTIALLY UNSTABLE in the record and its gain is reported as MSG = |S21|/|S12|, never as achievable gain. Cells are never excluded. k is reported against row 6, not claimed: the ideal-element circuit has no parasitic, no package and no layout, so its out-of-band k is optimistic by construction.

Operating-point method: `op` at each PVT point (self-heating selft=1 on, thermal node v(xdut.xqN.t) is dTj); per-device V_CE, V_BE, I_C, I_C/(3 mA x Nx), dTj and an fT estimate gm/(2 pi (cbe+cbex+cbc+cbcx+cbep+cbcp)) from the operating-point model parameters, each compared in the record with row 17 (V_CE <= 1.4 V, V_CE in the card's 0.4-2.0 V window), the card box (V_BE 0.65-0.96 V, I_C < 3 mA x Nx) and fT > 21.2 GHz. Supply 2.75 V is nominal +10 % of 2.5 V and is above row 17's 2.5 V rail ceiling: reported as an EXCURSION, not dropped and not merged into a pass; whether it is in scope is an open operator question.

IDEAL / BEHAVIORAL MATCHING: Cshunt + Lin (input) and Lfeed + Rd + Cm (output) are ideal lossless L/C (and one damping resistor Rd). No PDK inductor model exists for SG13G2 (confirmed absent in IHP-Open-PDK -- see sg13g2-vco's known_model_gaps note, restated in sim/README.md), so no inductor model of any kind is used or substituted: ideal ngspice L/C carry no loss, Q, self-resonance or layout parasitic. Values were sized at the DRAFT band centre from the bare stage's small-signal impedance (design/lna_stage1.md) and are NOT re-tuned per corner, so the process/temperature/supply spread in S11/S22/S21 includes match detuning. They are a behavioral placeholder until the passive study lands.

Rbias/Rd/R1b/R2b/Rref/Rer and the ideal Rs2 load are noisy at each corner's .temp and are part of the measured input-referred noise (Rs1 is the noiseless reference, issue #22). Rd (output damping) sits after the gain and mainly costs gain; it is listed so the NF number is not mistaken for a lossless-output figure.

No klayout-tools gap was hit by the schematic/netlist/simulation work itself (this bench does no layout/DRC/LVS). Fleet-submission friction (default runner-version enforcement against an older fleet runner; `stage_model_inputs` against that runner failing with a model-library path error) is described in the PR.
